picks.title: Hackers exploit trusted AWS access to breach multiple cloud environments
picks.summary: A threat actor used compromised identity and access management (IAM) credentials for a Qubole big data platform s AWS account to access and exfiltrate data from multiple customers AWS environments. [...]

picks.title: Software engineer Rickrolls his Prusa 3D printer via remote code execution exploit
picks.summary: A software engineer demonstrated the ability to Rickroll a 3D printer via remote code execution (RCE). This security flaw has been fixed in the latest Prusa software.

picks.title: Critical Xen Orchestra auth bypass flaw exploited to hijack VM servers
picks.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Xen Orchestra is being actively exploited in attacks that could grant administrator privileges and allow takeover of XCP-ng virtualization hosts. [...]

picks.title: Near AI Breach Exposes User Details and Data From 18 AI Agents
picks.summary: An SGLang flaw let an attacker reach internal systems and potentially view confidential AI requests, exposing the limits of hardware-backed privacy protections.

picks.title: Railway breach leads to $740,000 in fraudulent AI charges
picks.summary: Cloud hosting provider Railway says hackers exploited vulnerabilities in its infrastructure to steal customer authentication secrets and generate approximately $740,000 in fraudulent AI usage, potentially exposing credentials for up to 100,000 workspaces. [...]

picks.title: Artex: The AI Pen-Test Tool Hackers Turned Into a Weapon
picks.summary: Forks of the open source Artex framework, along with 45 similar pen-testing tools, remain capable of executing credential attacks and cloud breaches at machine speed across multiple industries.

picks.title: Japanese furniture giant Nitori says hackers stole 37.6M customer records
picks.summary: Nitori, a major Japanese furniture and home accessories retailer, discovered that an attacker accessed a system on its network and may have stolen 37.62 million customer records. [...]

picks.title: All net-connected vehicles from two major automakers allowed hackers to remotely unlock doors and start the engine
picks.summary: Any net-connected vehicle from two automakers could be remotely opened and started — now-patched failures with API backend security showcase a lack of 101-level best practices
